title: Arithmetic level raising, diagonal reciprocity and Rankin–Selberg Selmer ranks
summary: Extend the Selmer producer by native unitary arithmetic level raising, diagonal Abel–Jacobi classes and the two unequal-strength explicit reciprocity laws, ending in conditional and established-domain Selmer rank zero/one theorems. Missing accepted supplier sections and the rank-(2,3) proof are explicit gaps.

layers.title: Coefficient algebra, local predicates and admissibility

targets.name: lambdaExponent
targets.statement: For a commutative ring O, an ideal λ and an O-module M, define expλ(x) in ℕ∪{∞} as the infimum of the nonnegative e for which every element of λᵉ annihilates x. For a principal maximal ideal (π) this is the least e with πᵉx=0. Define ordλ(x) as the supremum of the nonnegative e with x∈λᵉM. Use ideal powers, so the definition is independent of a chosen uniformizer.

locator.where: Definition 2.1.6, p. 12; ltxzz line 549

api.name: lambdaExponent_le_iff
api.statement: expλ(x)≤e iff λᵉx=0, for e∈ℕ.

api.name: lambdaExponent_map_le
api.statement: For an O-linear map f, expλ(f x)≤expλ(x); equality holds for injective f.

api.name: lambdaExponent_unit_smul
api.statement: Multiplication by a unit preserves the exponent.

api.name: lambdaOrder_iso
api.statement: Module isomorphisms preserve ordλ; over a DVR ordλ(πᵃu in O)=a for u a unit.

api.name: lambdaExponent_reduction
api.statement: In O/πᵐ, exp(πᵃu)=m−a for 0≤a≤m and u a unit.

tests.name: exponent_ramified
tests.statement: In any DVR O, expπ(π in O/π³)=2; replacing π by the rational prime gives the wrong value in a ramified DVR.

tests.name: exponent_zero
tests.statement: expλ(0)=0 and ordλ(0)=∞; in a nonzero domain exp(1 in O)=∞.

tests.name: exponent_field
tests.statement: For λ=O, expλ(x)=∞ for x≠0, whereas λ=0 gives exponent 1 for x≠0. These boundary values distinguish ideal powers from an unspecified valuation.

tests.name: order_DVR
tests.statement: For any DVR O and uniformizer π, ordπ(π²u in O)=2 for a unit u; ordπ(u)=0.

tests.name: order_congruence
tests.statement: In O/π³, ordπ(π)=1 and ordπ(0)=∞.

tests.name: order_unit_ideal
tests.statement: For λ=O every x lies in every λᵉM, so ordλ(x)=∞, even when x≠0.

targets.proofSketch: Ideal-power monotonicity and the well-ordering of ℕ give the exponent API; linear maps preserve annihilation and λ-power divisibility. No finite generation is needed.
targets.adversarial: Zero module; λ=0,O; field; ramified and equal-characteristic DVR. The exponent of zero is 0, and infinity is retained.

targets.name: isFrobeniusWeaklySemisimple
targets.statement: For a finitely generated module M over L finite over ℤℓ or ℚℓ, with continuous action of an arbitrary topological group Γ, define weak semisimplicity to mean that the natural inclusion-to-quotient map M^Γ→M_Γ is an isomorphism. For a procyclic Γ this concerns the generalized eigenvalue-1 part; it does not assert semisimplicity of the entire representation.

locator.where: Definition 2.1.2 and Lemmas 2.1.3–2.1.5, pp. 11–12; ltxzz line 493

api.name: weaklySemisimple_iff_surjective
api.statement: When Γ≃Ẑ, for these noetherian modules the natural map is an isomorphism iff it is surjective.

api.name: weaklySemisimple_subquotient
api.statement: Finite sums preserve weak semisimplicity for arbitrary Γ; Γ-stable subquotients do so when Γ≃Ẑ.

api.name: weaklySemisimple_lift
api.statement: For Γ≃Ẑ and M finite free over Oλ, if its reduction is weakly semisimple and dim_E(M_E)^Γ≥dim_k(M_k)^Γ, then M is weakly semisimple and these dimensions are equal.

api.name: weaklySemisimple_iso
api.statement: Intertwining isomorphisms identify the natural maps.

tests.name: weak_trivial
tests.statement: The trivial action on O and on the zero module is weakly semisimple: the natural map is the identity.

tests.name: weak_jordan
tests.statement: Over 𝔽₃, for F=[[1,1],[0,1]], the natural map ker(F−1)→coker(F−1) is zero between one-dimensional spaces, so weak semisimplicity fails.

tests.name: weak_nonunit
tests.statement: Over ℤ₃, F=4 on a rank-one lattice has invariants 0 and coinvariants ℤ/3, so it is not weakly semisimple although F is diagonal over ℚ₃.

tests.name: cochain_sign
tests.statement: For the sign action of C₂ on ℤ, d0(1) at the nontrivial element is −2.

targets.proofSketch: Use the exact kernel/cokernel sequence of F−1 and the noetherian surjective-endomorphism criterion. For lifting, compare invariant ranks, reduce modulo λ, and use Nakayama.
targets.adversarial: Trivial Γ, rank zero and rank one, Jordan block and integral nonunit eigenvalue difference; no arbitrary nonnoetherian extension is asserted.

targets.name: satakeLocalConditions
targets.statement: For a nonzero commutative ring L, a unit q∈L and a monic degree-N polynomial P with N≥1 and P(T)=(−T)ᴺP(T⁻¹) as a Laurent-polynomial identity, define four predicates: odd Tate genericity is invertibility of P′(1); odd intertwining genericity is invertibility of P(−q); even level-raising specialness is P(q)=0 and invertibility of P′(q); even intertwining genericity is invertibility of P(−1). The parity requirement is part of each predicate.

locator.where: Definition 3.1.5 and Remark 3.1.6, pp. 23–24; ltxzz line 1044

api.name: satakeConditions_map
api.statement: A unital ring map preserves each predicate, with the target nonzero; transport the Laurent identity and monicity.

api.name: satakeConditions_local_iff_residue
api.statement: Over a commutative local ring, unit evaluations are equivalent to nonzero residue evaluations; the equation P(q)=0 is still required in the original ring.

api.name: satakeConditions_split_iff
api.statement: Over a splitting field, P′(a)≠0 at a root means a has multiplicity one; evaluations detect excluded roots without assuming distinctness of other roots.

api.name: satakeTensor
api.statement: For reciprocal polynomials presented by invertible root multisets, the polynomial of pairwise products is reciprocal and independent of splitting extension and root order.

tests.name: satake_even_F7
tests.statement: Over 𝔽₇ with q=2, P=(T−2)(T−4)=T²+T+1 has P(q)=0, P′(q)=5 and P(−1)=1; it is level-raising special and intertwining generic.

tests.name: satake_odd_F7
tests.statement: Over 𝔽₇ with q=2, P=(T−1)(T−3)(T−5)=T³+5T²+2T−1 has P′(1)=1 and P(−2)=0; Tate genericity holds and intertwining genericity fails.

tests.name: satake_collision
tests.statement: P=(T−1)² at q=1 fails even specialness over a field. Over 𝔽₂, P=T−1 is odd Tate generic but P(−1)=0. Modulo π², having P(q)=0 only modulo π does not establish specialness modulo π².

targets.proofSketch: Expand root products and use the derivative product rule. Descend symmetric expressions; invertibility transports along ring maps. The repeated-root test enforces the derivative condition.
targets.adversarial: q=1; characteristic 2 and 3; zero ring excluded to make degree and root language meaningful; nonreduced rings retained. Odd rank-one tests are algebraic checks, not automorphic endpoints.

targets.name: unitaryHeckeEigenvalues
targets.statement: For the unramified unitary group of rank N over the unramified quadratic local extension, normalize convolution by vol(K°)=1 and use the spherical Satake map of Construction 3.1.8. For reciprocal roots {aᵢ,aᵢ⁻¹}, the even-rank operator I° has value q^(r²)∏ᵢ(aᵢ+aᵢ⁻¹+2); (q+1)R°−I° has value −q^(r²)∏ᵢ(aᵢ+aᵢ⁻¹−q−q⁻¹). In odd rank 2r+1, I° has value q^(r²+r)∏ᵢ(aᵢ+aᵢ⁻¹+q+q⁻¹), and T° has value q^(r²+r)∏ᵢ(aᵢ+aᵢ⁻¹−2). Operators are the actual double-coset sums of §§B.2–B.4, including their transpose correspondences.
hypotheses: q is invertible in the coefficient ring; roots are units with the displayed inverse pairing.

locator.where: Construction 3.1.8; Propositions B.3.5 and B.4.3; ltxzz line 1086; ltxzz line 8157; ltxzz line 8400

tests.name: hecke_rank2
tests.statement: For r=1, q=3, a=3 in ℚ, I°=16 and (q+1)R°−I°=0. This fixes the negative product and volume normalization.

tests.name: hecke_rank3
tests.statement: For r=1, q=3, a=2 in ℚ, T°=9/2 and I°=105/2; the two operators are different.

tests.name: hecke_bad_denominator
tests.statement: The q⁻¹ formula is unavailable when q=0 in L; no division by q+1 is used to define the operators.

targets.proofSketch: Apply the supplied spherical Satake isomorphism to the explicitly finite double-coset sums. The scalar identities follow from their symmetric root expressions; Propositions B.3.5 and B.4.3 supply the arithmetic normalization.
targets.adversarial: r=0 formal empty product, r=1, q=1, nonunit q; neither intertwiners nor periods are assigned an unnamed unit.

targets.name: specialInertPlace
targets.statement: For a CM extension F/F⁺ and a finite place v of F⁺, define special inertness by inertness in F, an odd underlying rational prime p unramified in F, and F⁺ᵥ≃ℚp. Define very special inertness by also requiring a place of F⁺rflx above v with the same completion ℚp; Fᵣflx is generated by F and the reflex fields of all CM types of F.

locator.where: Definitions 3.3.1–3.3.4, p. 28; ltxzz line 1280; ltxzz line 1293

api.name: verySpecialInert_isSpecial
api.statement: Very special inertness implies special inertness.

api.name: verySpecialInert_of_reflexive
api.statement: When Fᵣflx=F the two predicates coincide.

api.name: specialInert_residue
api.statement: A special inert place has Fᵥ the unramified quadratic extension of ℚp, with residue size p².

api.name: specialInert_transport
api.statement: Field isomorphisms preserving the CM involution transport both predicates and their local embeddings.

tests.name: special_Qi_3
tests.statement: For F=ℚ(i), v=(3) is very special inert, and the residue field in F has 9 elements.

tests.name: special_Qi_split
tests.statement: For ℚ(i), v=(5) is split and v=(2) is ramified and even; neither is special inert.

tests.name: special_residue_degree
tests.statement: An inert place with [F⁺ᵥ:ℚp]=2 fails special inertness even when p is odd and unramified; an empty excluded set does not remove this condition.

targets.proofSketch: The first two clauses are logical consequences; the local degree statement uses unramified local extensions and inertness. Reflexive closure is imported, not reconstructed.
targets.adversarial: p=2,3, split/ramified/inert and degree two over ℚp. No residue-degree-one hypothesis is deleted on the strength of Remark 3.3.5.

targets.name: rankinSelbergAdmissible
targets.statement: For the standing relevant pair and strong field E, define admissibility of λ|ℓ by the seven independent clauses L1–L7 recorded below. Choose stable lattices Rα in ρΠα,λ(rα), of ranks nα, with (1−α)-polarizations Ξα; admissibility is invariant under their homotheties, polarization units and basis changes. L1: ℓ>4n and ℓ unramified in F. L2: no place above ℓ lies in Σ⁺min. L3: ρΠ₀,λ⊗ρΠ₁,λ is absolutely irreducible. L4: both factors are residually absolutely irreducible. L5-1: on R̄₀⊗R̄₁ either the residual image contains a scalar different from 1, or the module is semisimple, has dimension ≤min((ℓ+1)/2,ℓ−3), and HomΓF(End(R̄),R̄)=0. L5-2: over F⁺rflx the image of (ρ̄₀+,ρ̄₁+,ε̄ℓ) contains (γ₀,γ₁,ξ) with ξ²≠1, γα in the conjugate component of order prime to ℓ, eigenvalue 1 simple in hγ₀, hγ₁ and their tensor, and no eigenvalues −1 in hγ₀ or −ξ in hγ₁. Here hγ is the GL component of γ². L6: the even polarized residual representation is rigid for (Σ⁺min,∅) and stays absolutely irreducible over F(ζℓ). L7: both residual Hecke characters are cohomologically generic.

locator.where: Definition 8.1.1 and Remark 8.1.2, pp. 131–132; ltxzz line 6368

api.name: admissible_iff_clauses
api.statement: Give separate constructors/projections L1–L7, L5-1 alternatives and the L5-2 image witness; no opaque big-image field.

api.name: admissible_change_basis
api.statement: Conjugation, lattice homothety and multiplying a polarization by a unit preserve the predicate.

api.name: admissible_polarized_tensor
api.statement: R=R₀⊗R₁ has R^c≃R∨(1) and R_E≃Vλ since r₀+r₁=n.

api.name: admissible_not_small_prime
api.statement: No coefficient prime above ℓ≤4n is admissible.

tests.name: admissible_n2_twist
tests.statement: For n=2, (n₀,n₁,r₀,r₁)=(2,3,1,1); the tensor has rank 6 and total twist 2, and ℓ=3 fails L1.

tests.name: admissible_scalar_identity
tests.statement: The identity scalar alone never witnesses the first branch of L5-1; ξ=1 or −1 never witnesses L5-2, including over 𝔽₂ and 𝔽₃.

tests.name: admissible_basis
tests.statement: Replacing the two bases by invertible matrices changes the image witness by conjugation and leaves all seven truth values unchanged.

tests.name: frobenius_inert_three
tests.statement: Arithmetic Frobenius on Eλ(1) at a special inert p=3 place of F acts by 9; geometric Frobenius acts by 1/9.

tests.name: polarization_square
tests.statement: In the polarized disconnected group γ=(I,−1)c has GL component of γ² equal to −I.

targets.proofSketch: Use the imported polarizable representation category, residual image and rigidity predicates. The tensor polarization adds the twists 1 and 0. Conjugacy transports all spectra and invariant Hom spaces.
targets.adversarial: n=0,1 excluded; n=2 retained; ℓ=2,3 excluded arithmetically; ramification of Eλ is allowed and distinct from ramification of ℓ in F.

layers.examples: The ring examples include ramified mixed-characteristic DVRs, equal-characteristic DVRs and nonreduced congruence rings. Arithmetic admissibility itself uses finite extensions of ℚℓ, never these substitute coefficient rings.

layers.title: Unitary integral models, incidence and the semistable product

targets.name: unitaryLevelRaisingDatum
targets.statement: For N≥2 put r=⌊N/2⌋. Bundle a relevant Π, strong E, sets Σ⁺min⊇Σ⁺Π, Σ⁺lr of inert places strongly disjoint from Σ⁺min (their underlying rational supports are disjoint), and Σ⁺⊇Σ⁺min∪Σ⁺lr; λ|ℓ with no ℓ-adic place in Σ⁺min and ℓ∤Nv((Nv)²−1) for v∈Σ⁺lr; m≥1; a standard definite V° of rank N with self-dual lattice away from these sets and infinity; and neat K°, hyperspecial elsewhere, transferable at Σ⁺min and special maximal at Σ⁺lr in even rank, where V° is nonsplit. Include a special inert p, all auxiliary CM-moduli data of §§3.5/5.1 and an indefinite uniformization datum. Require P1: p-adic places avoid Σ⁺; P2: ℓ∤p(p²−1); P3: a CM type Φ containing τ∞ with Qp^Φ=ℚp²; P4: even PΠ,p is special modulo λᵐ, odd PΠ,p is Tate generic modulo λ; P5: PΠ,p is intertwining generic modulo λ; P6 in even rank: restriction of the congruence Hecke ideal away from p gives the same quotient of (OE/λᵐ)[Sh(V°,K°)] as the full ideal. Define mΠ and nΠ as contractions, to the algebra away from Σ⁺ and p, of the kernels of φΠ modulo λ and λᵐ.

locator.where: §6.1 and Notation 6.1.3, pp. 106–107; ltxzz line 5136; ltxzz line 5164; ltxzz line 5195

api.name: levelDatum_ext
api.statement: Equality of the geometric, lattice, level, prime and coefficient fields determines equality; proof fields are irrelevant.

api.name: levelDatum_reduce
api.statement: For 1≤a≤m, reduction to λᵃ preserves the Satake equations and P6 by right exactness, with the corresponding reduced ideals.

api.name: levelDatum_ideal_maps
api.statement: For a Hecke module M, M/nΠ is its actual quotient; M[mΠ] denotes the simultaneous annihilator and M_mΠ the localization, with distinct coercions and comparison maps.

api.name: levelDatum_changeLevel
api.statement: Pullback/trace are defined for compatible neat levels; the target datum must separately satisfy P6, rather than inheriting it without proof.

tests.name: level_positive_exponent
tests.statement: m=0 is outside the datum; m=1 makes nΠ the residual contracted ideal.

tests.name: level_empty_lr
tests.statement: Σ⁺lr=∅ is permitted and imposes no nonsplit condition there; p must still satisfy P1–P6.

tests.name: level_not_scalar
tests.statement: A congruence P(p)=0 modulo λ but not modulo λ² supplies an m=1 test datum and fails the m=2 condition; a wrong residual-only definition accepts it.

targets.proofSketch: Form a dependent structure using the native models and Hecke characters. Kernels and contractions produce its ideals. Reduction uses quotient tensor products, without identifying localization with the eigenspace.
targets.adversarial: Empty raising set, m=0,1,2; nonneat levels rejected; no global good-reduction assumption; all ramified exceptional places remain present.

targets.name: unitaryBasicCorrespondence
targets.statement: For the smooth standard-indefinite integral PEL model M at a special inert p, over the CM auxiliary base Tp, realize the source S and isogeny correspondence S←π B→ι M of §4.3. Over any field κ containing the residue field and s∈S(κ), B_s is smooth projective geometrically irreducible of dimension ⌊(N−1)/2⌋; ι is locally a closed immersion of codimension ⌊N/2⌋. Its tangent bundle is Hom(ωA∨,τ∞,ker α*,τ∞/ωA∨,τ∞) and its normal bundle is Hom(ωA∨,τ∞,im α*,τ∞). The fibre is the hermitian Frobenius incidence variety DL(V_s,{,}_s,⌈(N+1)/2⌉).

locator.where: Definitions 4.3.1–4.3.4 and Theorem 4.3.5, pp. 38–41; ltxzz line 1788; ltxzz line 1871

api.name: basicCorrespondence_representable
api.statement: Represent S as finite étale over Tp and B by its isogeny moduli; the maps retain their universal quasi-p-isogeny.

api.name: basicCorrespondence_baseChange
api.statement: The correspondence and tangent/normal identifications commute with residue-field extension and prime-to-p level maps.

api.name: basicCorrespondence_uniformize
api.statement: A definite uniformization datum identifies S with the actual definite unitary double quotient, compatibly with Hecke correspondences.

tests.name: basic_N2
tests.statement: For N=2 the fibre has dimension 0 and codimension 1 in a dimension-1 special fibre.

tests.name: basic_N3
tests.statement: For N=3 the fibre has dimension 1 and codimension 1 in a dimension-2 special fibre.

tests.name: basic_empty_fibre
tests.statement: Over the empty indexing scheme B is empty; no basis of functions on a nonempty invented finite set is introduced.

targets.proofSketch: Use the native moduli problem to construct the quasi-isogeny, Grothendieck–Messing to compute its tangent and normal spaces, and the hermitian incidence variety to identify the fibre functor. Descent proves representability and uniformization.
targets.adversarial: N=2,3 and base extension; locally closed immersion is not upgraded to a global embedding at arbitrary level.

targets.name: unitarySemistableStrata
targets.statement: For the definite datum and CM-moduli data of §5.1, realize M with special components M° and M• and link M†=M°∩M• as scheme-theoretic strata. M is strictly semistable of relative dimension N−1; the reduced components are smooth and cover its special fibre. The balloon correspondence B°→M° is an isomorphism, with fibres ℙ(V_s) over points of S° in perfect residue fields; the link in a balloon fibre is the degree-(p+1) hermitian Fermat hypersurface. The link normal in the balloon component is O(p+1); its normal in the ground component is the dual O(−(p+1)). Over perfect residue fields κ, ground fibres B•_s are the projective smooth incidence varieties DL•(V_s,{,}_s), of dimension ⌊N/2⌋. Retain the tangent and normal maps from the universal isogenies, and the link fibre projective bundles of §5.5.

locator.where: Theorems 5.2.5, 5.3.4, 5.4.4 and 5.5.3; Corollary 5.3.5, pp. 57–69; ltxzz line 2653; ltxzz line 2823; ltxzz line 2901; ltxzz line 2985

api.name: semistableStrata_localEquation
api.statement: At a link point the completed local ring is W(κ)[[x₁,…,xN]]/(x₁xN−p); away from the link it is formally smooth.

api.name: semistableStrata_baseChange
api.statement: Strata, universal isogenies and their incidence maps commute with compatible level and residue-field changes.

api.name: semistableStrata_genericFiber
api.statement: After the specified indefinite uniformization choice, Mη≃Sh(V′,jK^pK′p)×F Tη; prove compatibility with specialization in ordinary and compact supports, including nonproper models.

tests.name: strata_node
tests.statement: For N=2 the link chart has xy=p, two multiplicity-one components at p=0 and a zero-dimensional intersection.

tests.name: strata_normal_sign
tests.statement: For p=3 and N=3 the link in ℙ² is a smooth quartic: its normal O(4) has degree 16; the ground normal O(−4) has degree −16. Exchanging the two reverses the self-intersection sign.

tests.name: strata_generic
tests.statement: After inverting p, xy=p is smooth and has no special-fibre link; retaining a singular generic-fibre link fails the test.

targets.proofSketch: The pairing on crystalline Dieudonné modules is diag(p,1,…,1). Orthogonal Hodge lifts give xy=p. Universal isogenies identify the two incidence fibres and their normal bundles. The generic-fibre moduli interpretation and specialization follow from the native-model comparison contract.
targets.adversarial: N=2,3; p=3; the two link normal bundles are dual, with opposite signs; nonproper ordinary versus compact-support specialization must be proved, not inferred from proper base change.

targets.name: unitaryLinkAndIntersection
targets.statement: For the strata of 2.3 and p-coprime coefficient L, balloon and link cohomology are free L-modules. If p+1 is a unit, restriction Hⁱ(M°)→Hⁱ(M†) is an isomorphism except in degrees N−2 and 2N−2. In even rank, Frobenius on Hᴺ⁻²(M†,L((N−2)/2)) is trivial. For two ground fibres over a perfect κ, their fibre product decomposes by relative positions 0≤j≤⌊N/2⌋−1 into DL• incidence varieties. The corresponding link indexing set has ∏_{i=1}^{⌊N/2⌋−j}(p^(2i−1)+1) points, and each link intersection fibre is ℙ of a vector space of dimension ⌊N/2⌋−j. The excess bundle on it is σ*H⊗O(1), with H the tautological subbundle.

locator.where: Lemma 5.6.2; Theorems 5.7.7–5.7.8, pp. 71, 75–78; ltxzz line 3349; ltxzz line 3518; ltxzz line 3722

tests.name: link_minimal
tests.statement: When ⌊N/2⌋−j=1 the link index has p+1 points and each projective fibre is ℙ⁰.

tests.name: link_degree_bad
tests.statement: When ℓ divides p+1 the asserted restriction isomorphism is not exported; freeness and the geometric degree statement retain their separate domains.

targets.proofSketch: Apply the incidence variety cohomology and projective-bundle formula fibrewise. Relative positions classify the isogeny fibre product, and the tangent cokernel identifies its excess intersection bundle.
targets.adversarial: Empty relative-position range and smallest fibre; p+1 is not inverted in the geometric constructions.

targets.name: unitaryIncidenceWeightComplex
targets.statement: For 2.3 define the six incidence Gysin/restriction maps by pullback from S°,S•, powers of the positive hyperplane class and pushforward from B°,B•. Form the weight spectral sequence of RΨL(r), with columns −1,0,1: E₁⁻¹,ᵠ=Hᵠ⁻²(M†,L(r−1)), E₁⁰,ᵠ=Hᵠ(M°⊔M•,L(r)), E₁¹,ᵠ=Hᵠ(M†,L(r)). Use d₁⁻¹=(m†°!,−m†•!) and d₁⁰=m†°*−m†•*. For even rank retain the increasing filtration F₋₁≃E₂¹,²ʳ⁻², gr₀≃H²ʳ⁻¹(M•,L(r)), gr₁≃E₂⁻¹,²ʳ and monodromy induced by the identity of H²ʳ⁻²(M†,L(r−1)). Define ∇₁ on E₂⁰,²ʳ and ∇₀ on ker d₁⁰,²ʳ by the linear combinations in Construction 5.9.4, preserving T°•,T•° and the factors (p+1)² and p+1.

locator.where: Constructions 5.8.3, 5.9.1, 5.9.4; Lemmas 5.9.2–5.9.3, pp. 79–87; ltxzz line 4023; ltxzz line 4055; ltxzz line 4110; ltxzz line 4213

api.name: weightComplex_incidenceMatrix
api.statement: In odd rank the pairing matrix is [[1,0,0],[0,−(p+1)²,T°•],[0,T•°,T•]]. In even rank the monodromy-incidence matrix is [[p+1,(p+1)²,−T°•],[(p+1)²,(p+1)³,−(p+1)T°•],[−T•°,−(p+1)T•°,R•]] for N≥4, with middle row/column zero in the N=2 variant except the displayed corner terms.

api.name: weightComplex_singularSequence
api.statement: If p²−1 is a unit, 0→F₋₁H¹(I,H²ʳ⁻¹(RΨL(r)))→H¹sing→H²ʳ⁻¹(M•,L(r−1))_F→0.

api.name: weightComplex_functorial
api.statement: The maps are Hecke equivariant and commute with compatible coefficient/level maps; ∇₁ kills boundaries and factors through Frobenius coinvariants.

tests.name: incidence_sign
tests.statement: For the two-component node, the alternating restriction sends (a,b) to a−b; its value on (1,0) is 1 and on (0,1) is −1.

tests.name: incidence_scalar
tests.statement: At p=3 the odd middle diagonal entry is −16 and the first even diagonal entry is 4; swapping the sign or deleting the degree factor fails.

tests.name: incidence_identity_mono
tests.statement: The monodromy map from the extreme graded term is induced by the identity on link cohomology, with its displayed Tate twist; it is zero on F₀.

targets.proofSketch: Apply the imported weight spectral sequence to the actual strata. The excess intersection and normal-bundle computations in 2.4 compute each matrix entry. The filtration and singular sequence follow by inertia cohomology with the stated Frobenius exclusions.
targets.adversarial: Two components; N=2 exceptional matrix; nonunit p²−1; cohomological shifts and increasing filtration fixed explicitly.

targets.name: unitaryProductResolution
targets.statement: For compatible rank-n and rank-(n+1) semistable data, form P=M_n×Tp M_n+1 and Q=Bl_{P°°}P, with its strict transforms and the strict transform QΔ of the diagonal graph. Q is strictly semistable of relative dimension 2n−1, with four component strata and a weight sequence in columns −2,…,2.
